 Order

The petitioners are the accused Nos.1 to 4 in C.C No.876/2024 on the file of the Judicial First Class Magistrate Court-II, Kayamkulam, arising out of Crime No.960/2024 of Kayamkulam Police Station, Alappuzha.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The offences alleged against the petitioners are under Section 498A read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act,1961.
2.

The prosecution case is that the 1 st accused being the husband of the defacto complainant and the other accused persons being his relatives, subjected her to cruelty both physically and mentally,
misappropriated her gold ornaments and demanded a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- towards dowry and thereby they are alleged to have committed the above offences.

3 . According to the learned counsel for the petitioners, all the allegations levelled against the petitioners are false and no such incident occurred, and therefore, he prayed for quashing all further proceedings against the petitioners.

sentences.text: 4. The petition was strongly opposed by the learned counsel for the defacto complainant/respondent No.2 as well as the learned 2025:KER:92659 Public Prosecutor.

5. According to the learned counsel for the 2 nd respondent and the learned Public Prosecutor, there are specific allegation to prove the offences alleged against the petitioners, and therefore, they prayed for dismissing the Crl.M.C.
6. On a perusal of the F.I. Statement, it can be seen that the defacto complainant is a Doctor like the 1 st petitioner.

In the F.I.Statement, it is specifically alleged that in connection with her marriage 177 sovereigns of gold ornaments in addition to two diamond necklace, four pairs of ear studs and a chain were given to her, that the 1st petitioner received the entire ornaments on the day next to the marriage for keeping in safe custody, that they demanded a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- for purchasing a flat for her sister-in-law and since the said demand was not materialised, she was subjected to cruelty both physically and mentally.
In the F.I.Statement, there is a specific allegation that on 31.12.2023, the 1 st petitioner demanded a sum of Rs.50,00,000/- as dowry and subjected her to mental cruelty.
On 9.1.2024, she returned to the residence of the petitioners during the night.

When petitioners 2 to 4 came to know that she returned to the matrimonial home, during the night itself,
they summoned her and 2025:KER:92659 questioned as to why she returned to the matrimonial home, that it is not a place of tavern for anybody and also that she was not expelled from the house only because it was night.

7. On a perusal of the above F.I.Statement, it can be seen that, there are prima facie materials against the petitioners to prove the allegations under Section 498A r/w 34 IPC as well as Sections 3 and 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act and as such the prayer for quashing the case as against the petitioners is liable to be rejected.
8.
In the result, this Crl.M.C is dismissed.

At this stage the learned counsel for the petitioners submitted that unless this Court makes it clear that the Trial Court should proceed with the case untrammelled by the observations made by this Court in this order, it may cause prejudice to the petitioners.

In the above circumstance, it is made clear that the observations made by the Court in this order are only prima facie findings for the purpose of disposal of this Cri.M.C and the Trial Court should dispose of the case, untrammelled by the observations made by this Court in this order, on merits, as per law.
Sd/-C.PRATHEEP KUMAR JUDGE ma/01.12.2025 2025:
